newsitem.title: VATICAN: Vatican condemns ETA kidnap of Basque politician.
newsitem.headline: Vatican condemns ETA kidnap of Basque politician.

text.p: The Vatican on Friday condemned the kidnapping of a Spanish politician by Basque separatist guerrillas who have threatened to kill him.

"It's an act of terrorism which threatens the life of the hostage, which is an affront to peaceful co-habitation and which offends the sentiments of the noble Spanish people," Vatican Secretary of State Cardinal Angelo Sodano wrote.

He said in a letter to the Roman Catholic bishop of Bilbao that Pope John Paul, who is on holiday in the Italian Alps, was saddened by news of the kidnapping of Miguel Angel Blanco, a Basque town councillor and member of the ruling Popular Party.

Sodano said the Pope condemned "this permanent form of violence which offends human and Christian conscience". The Pontiff was praying for Blanco, who was abducted on Thursday, and sent sympathy to his family.

Authorities said separatist group ETA (Basque Homeland and Freedom) had vowed to execute him unless about 500 ETA prisoners held throughout Spain were transferred by 4 p.m. (1400 GMT) on Saturday to institutions closer to the Basque region.
